findings.title: Successful cleanup batches are logged as errors and include entire ID lists
findings.body: The new cleanup path emits `Error` logs even when `fetchIDs` and deletion succeeded (`err` is nil), including for the terminating empty batch. It also attaches every selected ID to the log entry. With the configured batch size this can serialize and write tens of thousands of IDs per batch (the added test explicitly uses 32,767), producing very large error logs, false error alerts, and avoidable CPU/I/O on every cleanup run. Use an appropriate non-error level and log a bounded summary such as count (and only log the actual error when present). The equivalent calls in `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` have the same issue.

findings.title: The unrelated ticker change runs every cleanup job ten times more often
findings.body: Changing the cleanup ticker from ten minutes to one minute affects all jobs in `clean`, not only annotation cleanup: snapshot/version/image deletion, invite expiration, short-URL cleanup, and query-history retention and row-limit enforcement will now execute up to ten times as often. This can substantially increase database and filesystem load, and long-running cleanup cycles can become nearly continuous because another tick is already pending when a cycle completes. The PR does not scope or justify this behavioral change; retain the existing interval or make any desired annotation-specific scheduling change separately.
